## Triage order (batched into work items)

The top 10 isn't 10 tasks. It's five, because the findings cluster by file and share a fix.

**WI-0 — Write `AGENTS.md`** · `crime_00003` · effort: small
Do this first even though crimes ranks it #3. It's the multiplier: every fix below gets made by an agent that currently can't discover the build command, the layer boundaries, or which of the four names for `/settings/billing` is canonical. Cheapest item on the list, and it lowers the risk of everything after it.

**WI-1 — One time domain in `src/date.ts`** · `crime_00001`, `crime_00010` (+ free riders `crime_00012`, `crime_00018`, `crime_00026`, `crime_00027`)
Six of the 37 findings are the same file and the same root cause: no clock injection, no chosen time domain. Fixing them separately means touching `date.ts` six times. One pass — inject a clock, pick UTC for storage, convert at the display boundary — closes all six. `crime_00010` (same receiver `d` reads `getUTCFullYear()` at L9 and `getMonth()` at L41) is the one that silently produces wrong output today, not just untestable output.

**WI-2 — Make the invoice tests real** · `crime_00025`, `crime_00034` · **prerequisite, not optional**
`crime_00025` reports a test with *zero* assertions; `crime_00034` reports one with only weak matchers. Note the trap: every `src/billing.ts` finding carries `test_gap: 0` because the file *has* a test file. It has no meaningful coverage. Trust `weak_test_signal` over the `test_gap` score here — refactoring a 204-line function behind tests that assert nothing is the highest-actual-risk move available.

**WI-3 — Decompose `src/billing.ts`** · `crime_00005` (+ `crime_00013` clock, `crime_00035` God File, `crime_00015` `calculateRefundPreview` misnaming, `crime_00020` rule-in-a-comment)
Blocked on WI-2. `generateInvoice` at 204 lines is 3.4× the threshold, and the extraction is the natural carrier for the other four: pull the clock out (`crime_00013`, 7 more direct dates), split the file (`crime_00035`, 311 lines), rename `calculateRefundPreview` to disclose that it calls `saveRefundAudit`/`sendRefundEmail` (`crime_00015`), and encode "only owners can refund enterprise plans unless billing support approves" as a guard instead of a comment (`crime_00020`).

**WI-4 — Promote `"enterprise"` to a constant** · `crime_00004` · effort: small
Do it *before* WI-3, not after. The literal spans `src/api/plan.ts`, `src/billing.ts`, `src/jobs/plan-sync.ts`, `src/ui/pricing.ts` — four areas, four layers. Centralising it first means the billing refactor has one definition to move rather than four to keep in sync.

**WI-5 — One canonical name for `/settings/billing`** · `crime_00006` + `crime_00007` (+ related `crime_00019`)
These are one defect reported twice. The destination is called Plans, Billing, `PricingPage`, and Subscription across the route path, component name, `metadata.title`, `<title>`, and two nav files. Both findings sit at confidence 0.65–0.70, so verify before acting — but the evidence lists the divergent labels explicitly, and they don't look like false positives. `crime_00019` (Concept Alias Drift: account / organisation / team / workspace across 5 files) is the same disease at vocabulary scale; worth deciding the canonical term in the same sitting.

## Deferred

**`crime_00002`, `crime_00009`** — both `src/petty.ts`, both low severity, `blast_radius: 0`, confidence 0.73–0.74. `resolvePaymentResult` returning `{code, message, ok}` in one branch and `{permanent, url}` in another at 0% key overlap is a real contract smell, and a 6-field untyped `options` bag is a real discoverability problem for agents. Neither is worth a dedicated PR. Fix them the next time someone opens the file.

## Ignored

**`crime_00008` Sync I/O in Hot Path** — suppress with a reason, don't fix. The three sync calls are `existsSync`/`statSync`/`readFileSync` inside `loadPlanSchema`, which is a boot-time schema read. The detector's "hot path" claim isn't established by its own evidence: `blast_radius: 0`, no call-frequency signal, and a one-shot config load is the canonical case where sync I/O is fine and arguably preferable. This is a false positive for this call site.

Below the top 10 I'd also ignore `crime_00024` (Plural Mismatch), `crime_00028` (Unprefixed Boolean in `petty.ts`), and `crime_00036` (32×32 icon raster) — all naming/asset preference with no correctness consequence.

## Two things the ranking gets wrong here

**`crime_00017` (Localhost-on-Disk) is ranked #17 and is the most broken thing in the repo.** `src/api/files.ts:9` hardcodes `/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/schema.json`. That path exists on exactly one machine — it fails for every other developer, every CI runner, every deploy. It scores `agent_risk: 0.30` because it's *unambiguous to an agent*, which is exactly right for what agent risk measures and exactly wrong as a proxy for breakage. Same file, same story with `crime_00016` (`localhost:3000` at L8). Both are `effort: quick`. **Fix these first alongside WI-0** — they're a five-minute change that unbreaks the fixture for everyone but the author.

**Aggregate ranking ≠ triage order.** Agent risk sorts by "how likely is an agent to make a confident wrong edit here." That's the right default for `crimes scan`, but a triage plan also has to weigh sequencing (WI-0 before everything), safety gates (WI-2 before WI-3), and batching (six `date.ts` findings, one pass). Six of my top seven come from the tool's top ten — the ordering differs mostly in what I pulled forward to de-risk the rest.

**Verification:** after each work item, `crimes verdict --format json` should report `fixed > 0` and `new: 0`. If `new` is non-zero, the refactor introduced something — that's the signal to stop and look, and it's the one place this report *should* gate a merge.
